chapter: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
title: Adelaide Hall's pianists and Joe Turner
summary: They sort out that Tatum went to Europe with Adelaide Hall and then Joe Turner, the pianist who wrote Walking Through Heaven.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: Just before you get off of Art Tatum, you say he came here with Adelaide Hall.
That's right.
Do you remember, was it a duo? Did they have two piano players?
No.
Well, there was one piano player named Joe Turner that played with her. That was they were supposedly have gotten him the job with her and at one time they played together. Do you remember that?
No, I don't. You see, Art Tatum went to Europe with her but Art Tatum came back.
Right.
And then Joe went to Europe, you see.
But Joe was with her first, wasn't that --
Yeah. I think Joe was with her first and then he left her, you see, because at that time when I came to New York and Connie's Inn in '32 I met Joe Turner then. That's when he wrote --
Joe Turner, the pianist?
Yeah. That's when he wrote Walking Through Heaven and a couple of --
Is that his tune?
Oh, yes, oh, yes.
Yeah, "I'm walking through heaven with you."
That's right, yeah.
Oh, well, Don's -- Whose band did that?
Jimmie Lunceford.
Jimmie Lunceford's band did that?
That's right, when Henry Wells was singing with the band and before [Paul] -- I mean, before -- oh, what's the singer? -- Grissom. Before Dan Grissom.
Dan Grissom.
Yeah.
Yeah, we didn't mention the vocalists, like Dan Grissom.
Well, Henry Wells was a reasonable vocalist on that, you see. And --
Well, go ahead on with Tatum.
And so --
